project.name: AI Workspace (repo: figma-ai-executor; GitHub: Sabir59/auto-dev)
project.one_line: A local AI workforce platform: specialized Workers, grouped into Teams, operate inside real Workspaces (files, Git, Figma, browser) under limits enforced below the model, with every action observable and every result reviewable.

mission.problem: Chat assistants talk about work; organizations need AI that does real work inside their real systems, safely and accountably.
mission.for_whom_now: The owner and the MATW frontend team (first real environment).
mission.vs_chatbot: Acts through real tools on real resources; enforced boundaries; NEEDS instead of workarounds; recorded, resumable runs with snapshots.
mission.vs_claude_code: The runtime IS Claude Code (claude.exe). The product is the layer around it: workspaces with security profiles and run binding, worker definitions computing tools/context, Teams with shared context and enforced policies, adapters with their own enforcement, activity log, Git versions/explicit push, safe attachments and @ mentions.

design_principles: Build everything on pain. When we discover what is missing, build it.
No beautiful UI with fake functionality; every control has a real purpose
No placeholder features or invented capabilities
Prove capability through real execution: inspect -> test -> prove -> integrate
Security enforced below the model; the model is not the security boundary
Don't call anything secure/sandboxed/isolated/read-only unless a test demonstrates it
Workers specialize; Teams provide operational context; Workspace is the resource/security boundary
Capabilities narrow access; requirements are not authorization; missing access -> NEEDS
Reference shared knowledge, don't duplicate it
Don't build future infrastructure before current pain requires it
Report honestly: proven vs unproven vs failed
ux_principles: Make obvious: what exists, what can be done, active worker/team/workspace/mode, resources, what the AI is doing, what happened, what failed, what access is missing
No decorative controls, meaningless filters, fake buttons, inactive icons, empty sections
Keep the Stitch visual language (Geist/Geist Mono dark tokens)
Truthful labels: ENFORCED vs INSTRUCTION, WORKSPACE FILE vs UPLOADED, read-only view
